history.dynasty: Rebuilt repeatedly by Hindu rulers; present structure by the Government of India / Somnath Trust, 1947-1951 (Chalukya architectural style)
history.period: Legendary antiquity; destroyed and rebuilt many times; present temple 1947-1951
history.summary: Somnath at Prabhas Patan is the first of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva and is known as 'the Shrine Eternal'. Legend holds that the Moon God (Chandra/Soma) installed the first lingam here in gold to be freed of Daksha's curse; tradition says it was later rebuilt in silver by Ravana and in sandalwood by Krishna. The historic temple was destroyed and looted repeatedly — by Mahmud of Ghazni (1024), Alauddin Khilji's commander (1296/1297), Muzaffar Shah (1375), Mahmud Begada (1451) and Aurangzeb (1665/1706, per differing accounts) — and rebuilt by rulers including Vikramaditya of Ujjain, the Vallabhi kings, Bhimadeva of Anhilwada and Khangara of Junagadh. After Independence, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel mooted the reconstruction during the Junagadh integration (November 1947); after his death the work continued under K. M. Munshi, and President Rajendra Prasad performed the installation ceremony on 11 May 1951. The present sandstone temple stands on the Arabian Sea shore at the Triveni Sangam (confluence of the Kapila, Hiran and Saraswati rivers), and is also believed to be the place where Krishna ended his earthly lila. TOWN NOTE: CSV town 'Somnath' is the common name; the town is officially Prabhas Patan, Gir Somnath district, approx. 8 km from Veraval.

name: Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Prabhas Patan (commonly called Somnath) is a coastal pilgrimage town in Gir Somnath district, Gujarat, on the Arabian Sea at the Triveni Sangam — the confluence of the Kapila, Hiran and Saraswati rivers. About 8 km from the historic port city of Veraval, it is one of India's foremost Shiva pilgrimage centres and a major tourist destination, hosting the Somnath Jyotirlinga temple, an evening light-and-sound show, and the November Kartik Purnima fair.
